children.name: LLMOS: Project Blueprint & Startup Vision Project Name: Next Big Thing (Working Title) / LLMOS Core Mission: To build an OS-level AI assistant that executes multi-step workflows faster than a human can using a mouse and keyboard. 1. Executive Summary LLMOS (Large Language Model Operating System) is an Agentic AI layer that sits directly on top of the user's operating system. Instead of merely generating text, LLMOS translates natural language (specifically voice commands, leveraging models like Whisper) into executable actions. The ultimate goal is to create a frictionless, hands-free computing experience where users can queue up tasks asynchronously while focusing on deep work. 2. The "Aha!" Moment: Restricting the Use Case The AI graveyard is full of startups that promised to do everything and delivered nothing. LLMOS differentiates itself by strictly avoiding vague, open-ended commands and focusing intensely on specific, highly-structured daily workflows. The Anti-Goal (Vague/Impossible): "Build me Facebook." (Too broad, sets false expectations). The Sweet Spot (Developer Workflow): "Create a repo named 'Next Big Thing' and create a local copy in the Projects folder." The Sweet Spot (Productivity Workflow): "Open Notion, go to My Day template and add Chest day." 3. Technical Architecture & Strategy To achieve the necessary speed and reliability, the system architecture must bypass traditional, fragile automation methods. Table The Hybrid Execution Model LLMOS will primarily utilize the OS Accessibility Tree. This allows the AI to instantly parse the screen's DOM, calculate exact coordinates in milliseconds, and execute clicks/typing programmatically. For the minority of applications where developers have failed to implement proper accessibility tags (the "leftovers"), LLMOS will seamlessly fall back to a highly-optimized Computer Vision/Screenshot pipeline to bridge the gap. // LLMOS Decision Pipeline Command Received -> Parse Intent If Element in Accessibility Tree: Execute via OS GUI Tree (Latency: < 0.5s) Else: Capture Screenshot -> Locate Element -> Execute (Latency: ~2-3s) 4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) & User Experience North Star Metric: Time-to-Execution. The total time from voice command to action completion MUST be faster than a user executing the same task manually with a mouse and keyboard. Asynchronous Queuing: Users should be able to rattle off multiple requests (e.g., "Draft an email to John, then open my calendar and block off 3 PM") and have LLMOS queue and execute them in the background without freezing the user's workflow. 5. Next Steps for MVP Define the target operating system for V1 (macOS vs. Windows). Build the parser for the Accessibility Tree on the chosen OS.
